scenes.tts: Cells break down food to build A T P, a molecule that carries energy to cell work. With oxygen, most A T P is made in the mitochondria. This is cellular respiration. It matters because every working cell needs energy. A muscle cell pulls. A nerve cell pumps charged particles. Cells build proteins.

Keep the established concept colors.

scenes.tts: Glucose is a sugar. With oxygen, it becomes carbon dioxide and water. Much of the released energy is captured in A T P. Some leaves as heat. The first steps happen in the cytoplasm. Later steps happen in mitochondria, organelles in plant, animal and fungal cells. Plants respire too.
scenes.visual: Show glucose plus oxygen becoming carbon dioxide and water. Trace energy into ATP and heat. Within a cell, locate the first steps in the cytoplasm and later steps in the mitochondrion. Show plant, animal and fungal cell labels; include a plant cell with mitochondria.

scenes.tts: A T P has three phosphate groups in a row. When A T P reacts with water, the end phosphate group comes off. What is left is A D P, with two phosphate groups. The whole reaction releases energy that the cell uses for work. Breaking a bond takes energy. A T P is not energy. It is a molecule that carries energy.
scenes.visual: Show ATP with three phosphate groups reacting with water to give ADP and a separate phosphate. Connect an energy arrow from the whole reaction to cell work. Label the whole reaction as releasing energy; show a brief note that breaking a bond takes energy. End with ATP as a molecule that carries energy.

scenes.tts: Putting a phosphate group back onto A D P takes energy. Cellular respiration supplies that energy. So A T P and A D P go round in a cycle. Cell work turns A T P into A D P. Respiration turns A D P back into A T P. A cell keeps only a small supply of A T P, so it rebuilds it all the time.
scenes.visual: Show a loop between ATP and ADP plus phosphate. Label ATP reacting with water as supplying energy for cell work. Label rebuilding ATP as requiring energy supplied by respiration. Animate repeated rebuilding beside a small ATP supply.
scenes.narration: Putting a phosphate group back onto ADP takes energy. Cellular respiration supplies that energy. So ATP and ADP go round in a cycle. Cell work turns ATP into ADP. Respiration turns ADP back into ATP. A cell keeps only a small supply of ATP, so it rebuilds it all the time.

scenes.tts: Aerobic means using oxygen. Anaerobic means without oxygen. Without oxygen, muscle cells and yeast use fermentation. The S O L calls this anaerobic respiration. With oxygen, an animal cell gets about thirty to thirty-two A T P per glucose. Fermentation gives only two. In muscle, fermentation makes lactate. In yeast, it makes ethanol and carbon dioxide. The carbon dioxide forms the bubbles that make dough rise.
scenes.visual: Show aerobic as using oxygen and anaerobic as without oxygen. Compare about 30 to 32 ATP per glucose for aerobic respiration in an animal cell with 2 for fermentation. Label the SOL term anaerobic respiration. Branch fermentation into muscle producing lactate and yeast producing ethanol plus carbon dioxide bubbles in dough. Do not show an enzyme-speed comparison or sprint timing.

scenes.tts: Photosynthesis uses light energy to build glucose from carbon dioxide and water. It releases oxygen. Respiration breaks glucose down with oxygen into carbon dioxide and water. Plants do both. The atoms go round and round. Energy arrives as light and leaves as heat. Along the way, A T P carries energy from food to cell work.
